correctness.rationale: The source uses exactly the defining equality between prefix one-counts and maximal linear-factor counts for every length and every cut. My independently written enumerator tested all 2^n rooted words and all rotations for each n=1..11, with 0 bad necklaces through n=10 and precisely the stated three at n=11; 33 rooted words. Read the source gap-composition proof: a shortest span of k+1 consecutive ones is determined by k adjacent gaps and its prefix competitor; the last circular gap is excluded after the cut. The included witness CSV contains 33 explicit prefix/factor comparisons. The all-n witness is proved separately: zero-start cuts fail at length 1, starts at positions 3,5,7 fail due to later 11, start 9 fails by 10101 against 11000, and start 10 fails by 101 against 100. Extra n=1000 check is corroborative, not an unbounded proof.
